case_title.quote: SUNIL DAMODAR GAIKWAD v. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: The appellant was prosecuted for causing the death of his wife and two sons

accused_gender.quote: The appellant was married to a woman named Sangita.
accused_gender.reason: Accused is male (father, husband); the text uses male pronouns.

accused_age.reason: No age is given for this accused; the only age reference (thirty-five) concerns Sushil Kumar's case.

accused_religion.reason: Religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.quote: He was a tailor by profession and employed as such in a cloth shop.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Judgment repeatedly describes the family as poor and the accused as poverty-stricken.

previous_criminal_record.quote: The accused had no prior criminal record.
previous_criminal_record.reason: Judgment expressly states no prior criminal record.

victim_gender.correct_value: Multiple victims: wife and daughter female; two sons male
victim_gender.quote: his wife Sangita and his two sons ... On his daughter Gaitri alias Pooja also
victim_gender.reason: Victims include both males (two sons) and females (wife, daughter); single value is incomplete.

victim_age.reason: No victim ages are given; 35 appears to be borrowed from an unrelated accused.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: his wife Sangita and his two sons ... On his daughter Gaitri alias Pooja also
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Spouse is correct for the wife, but the sons and daughter were the accused's children.

offence_category.quote: The appellant was prosecuted for causing the death of his wife and two sons, and attempting to kill his daughter
offence_category.reason: Murder and attempted murder are the offence categories.

statutory_provisions.quote: The appellant faced trial under Section 302 read with Section 307 of IPC.
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections 302 and 307 IPC are the statutory provisions.

weapon.quote: killed his wife and two sons with a pair of scissors
weapon.reason: Weapon was a pair of scissors.

evidence_type.quote: PW1 ... PW3 is the doctor ... Article No. 6, scissors
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness testimony, medical evidence and weapon recovery are all relied on.

confession.correct_value: Police statement (Exhibit 29) recorded and referred to; judgment does not call it a confession
confession.quote: The statement-Exhibit No.29 was recorded by him and appellant signed the same.
confession.reason: A police statement was relied on, but the judgment never describes it as a confession.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Not stated by court; facts include multiple deaths and use of scissors
aggravating_circumstances.quote: inflicted multiple stab injuries causing their instantaneous death
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Facts support multiple deaths and sharp weapon, but the court identifies no aggravating factors itself.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Economic and psychic compulsions, poverty, no prior criminal record, possibility of reform
mitigating_circumstances.quote: The appellant had in fact intended to wipe out the whole family including himself on account of abject poverty.
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Poverty and no record are supported, but no suicide attempt by the accused is found; remorse is not expressly stated.

trial_court_outcome.quote: The trial court convicted the appellant u/ss 302 and 307 IPC and sentenced him to death under the first count and life imprisonment under the second one.
trial_court_outcome.reason: Conviction and sentences match the judgment.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: High Court confirmed death sentence under s.302 and dismissed appeal confirming s.307 conviction and sentence
high_court_outcome.quote: On reference, the High Court confirmed the death sentence.
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court did not reject the outcome; it confirmed the death sentence and dismissed the appeal.

final_outcome.quote: while upholding the conviction of the appellant under Section 302 and Section 307 of IPC, we modify the sentence
final_outcome.reason: Conviction upheld; sentence modified, so 'convicted' is accurate.

offence_finally_established.quote: while upholding the conviction of the appellant under Section 302 and Section 307 of IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Murder and attempt to murder convictions were upheld.

imprisonment_type.correct_value: Life imprisonment (s.302) and seven years imprisonment (s.307)
imprisonment_type.quote: (a) For offence under Section 302 of IPC, the appellant is sentenced to life imprisonment. (b) ... imprisonment for a period of seven years.
imprisonment_type.reason: Life is correct for s.302 but the s.307 seven-year term is omitted.

imprisonment_years.correct_value: 7 (for s.307; life for s.302 has no fixed term)
imprisonment_years.quote: (b) For offence under Section 307 of IPC, the appellant is convicted to imprisonment for a period of seven years.
imprisonment_years.reason: Judgment states seven years for s.307, so null is wrong.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is mentioned in the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Accused denied everything in his Section 313 statement; police statement was not a denial
neutral_facts.quote: the appellant, in his statement uls. 313 Cr.P.C., simply denied everything and did not lead any evidence.
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate, but the denial is wrongly attributed to the police statement rather than the Section 313 statement.

offence_severity.correct_value: Trial court sentences: death under s.302; life imprisonment under s.307
offence_severity.quote: The trial court convicted the appellant u/ss 302 and 307 IPC and sentenced him to death under the first count and life imprisonment under the second one.
offence_severity.reason: Presents sentences as statutory minimum/maximum; judgment states only the imposed sentences.

attempt_completion.correct_value: Murder completed; attempt to murder on daughter (not completed)
attempt_completion.quote: pressed her mouth with pillow but she did not succumb to death
attempt_completion.reason: 'Completed' fits the murders but ignores that the s.307 attempt on the daughter failed.

physical_harm.quote: causing their instantaneous death. On his daughter Gaitri alias Pooja also, he inflicted stab injuries.
physical_harm.reason: Deaths of wife and sons and injuries to daughter are supported.

number_of_offences.quote: while upholding the conviction of the appellant under Section 302 and Section 307 of IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Two counts were charged and both convictions upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No financial or property loss is discussed.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Judgment records he decided to finish the family and intended to wipe them out; premeditation not expressly found
premeditation_planning.quote: he decided to finish the entire family including himself
premeditation_planning.reason: Judgment records a decision and intent, so 'not found' overstates the absence of planning.

motive.quote: He had in fact intended to wipe out the whole family including himself on account of abject poverty.
motive.reason: Abject poverty and economic stress are identified as the motive.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: The prosecution examined nine witnesses and based mainly on the version of PW1-Gaitri
key_evidence_accepted.reason: PW1's account, PW4 corroboration and accused's statement content are relied on.

witness_credibility.quote: Gaitri alias Pooja was clear and consistent during the investigation as well as before the Sessions Court.
witness_credibility.reason: Judgment finds PW1 consistent and PW4 corroborative; evidence established guilt beyond doubt.

post_offence_conduct.quote: he gave her water to drink ... went straight to the police station and gave a statement of what he had done.
post_offence_conduct.reason: Court notes the change of heart and reporting to police; remorse is an interpretation the court itself draws.

trial_duration.quote: The Court ... passed the High Court judgment dated 23.09.2010
trial_duration.reason: Value gives judgment dates, not trial duration; no trial duration is stated.

legal_representation.quote: Ramesh Chandra Mishra, Dr. Meera Agarwal for the Appellant. Sushil Karanjkar, Asha Gopalan Nair for the Respondent.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered; investigation conducted by PW8; charge sheet not mentioned
investigation_status.reason: FIR and trial are supported, but charge sheet filing is not stated.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural irregularity is noted in the judgment.

appeal_history.quote: The appeal filed by the appellant before the High Court was dismissed confirming the conviction and sentence under Section 307.
appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.reason: The judgment does not record prosecution arguments; only the lower courts' views are described.

defence_argument.correct_value: Counsel mainly canvassed for commutation of the death sentence; specific arguments on compulsions not recorded
defence_argument.quote: the learned counsel appearing for the appellant was mainly canvassing for commuting the death sentence
defence_argument.reason: Commutation request is supported, but the poverty and rarest-of-rare arguments are not recorded as counsel's.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the rule is life imprisonment for murder, and death is the exception for which special reasons are to be stated.
legal_principle_applied.reason: Rule-exception principle under s.354(3) is applied.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Bachan Singh; Machhi Singh; Shankar Kisanrao Khade; Ediga Anamma; Sushil Kumar; Dalbir Singh (1979) 3 SCR 1059; Gopal Vinayak Godse
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Dalbir Singh vs. State of Punjab 1979 (3) SCR 1059 = AIR 1979 SC 1384 - relied on.
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Most precedents are correct, but Dalbir Singh, relied on per headnote and para 22, is omitted.

sentencing_rationale.quote: The 'individually inconclusive and cumulatively marginal facts and circumstances' tend towards awarding lesser sentence of life imprisonment.
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale matches the court's reasoning in para 26.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: The possibility of reforming and rehabilitating the accused cannot be ruled out. The accused had no prior criminal record.
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Listed mitigating factors match the court's findings.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Not stated (court identifies no aggravating factors for this accused)
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Judgment does not expressly say there were no aggravating factors; 'None' overstates the court's findings.

other_sentence_order.quote: in case the sentence of imprisonment for life is remitted or commuted to any specified period ... the sentence of imprisonment under Section 307 of IPC shall commence thereafter.
other_sentence_order.reason: Describes the commutation and consecutive-commencement direction accurately.
